records.region: Seward Peninsula, Alaska: Caviar Creek–Koyuk River corridor and Koyuk delta
records.geographic_disambiguation: Representative receiving-river/system identity for the connected selected Caviar approach–Koyuk corridor and delta. Koyuk River is not assigned as the scalar name of the initial unnamed feeder, the Caviar tributary or every delta island/pond.
records.completion_scope: Four overlapping original maps were visually read across all 54 stored parts of the one selected mainstem: chosen western opening, feeder and named tributary, receiving junction, upper and middle river, all intervening joins, pond-rich meander belts, lower river and the actual interior-delta endpoint. Connected valley, channel and delta correspondence is established at ordinary corridor scale. Local valley-side displacement, straightened meanders and the terminal island/bend shortcut are explicit generalization limits; exact banks, present distributary choice and a precise sea-mouth vertex are not asserted.
records.supported_name_scope: Caviar Creek for its separately labelled upstream tributary; Koyuk River for the receiving upper, middle and lower river and delta. The short western opening remains unnamed at this evidence scope.

records.region: La Laguna, Durango and Coahuila, Mexico
records.material_pending_reason: The western approach, central natural-versus-managed connections, cross-sheet northern course and actual terminal were not established from material actually read before the publication stop.
records.geographic_disambiguation: No natural-river name is supported for the selected whole system by the material actually inspected. This is incomplete source correspondence, not a conclusion that the feature is unnamed.
records.completion_scope: All selected parts were considered, but only prior lawful G1309 overview and legend observations were available. No detailed selected through-link or terminal correspondence was completed before the publication cancellation.
records.supported_name_scope: No natural-river name is supported for the selected whole system by the material actually inspected. This is incomplete source correspondence, not a conclusion that the feature is unnamed.

scope_limits: All 37 selected parts are accounted for in the component list, but none has completed ordinary selected-route correspondence.
Possible natural-channel, dry-plain, impoundment or managed-channel passages remain unestablished; no current operation or exact-bank assertion is needed or made.
Search-indexed labels and other discovery results are not used as river-name or continuity evidence.
No whole-system identity, local reach name or receiving feature name is supported at a sufficient selected-route scope.

records.region: Alaska: Kashunuk–Aphrewn corridor in the Yukon–Kuskokwim delta
records.geographic_disambiguation: Representative receiving-river/system identity for the connected selected Kashunuk-to-Aphrewn route. Aphrewn River is supported for the lower receiving reach and actual selected terminal; it is not assigned to the long upstream Kashunuk reaches.
records.completion_scope: Four overlapping original map views were visually read across all 54 parts of the one selected mainstem, including the chosen Kashunuk opening, large upper and middle bends, divided-channel joins, Nanvaranak Choa widening, broad southern Kashunuk passage, lower branch transition, Aphrewn reach and actual stored endpoint. Ordinary connected-corridor correspondence is complete. The actual endpoint is a position within the mapped Aphrewn channel rather than a demonstrated natural ocean mouth. Model bend and island shortcuts do not establish separate waterways along every rendered segment.
records.supported_name_scope: Kashunuk River for the selected upper and middle meandering delta channel, its connected widening and lower branching approach; Aphrewn River for the selected southward receiving channel and actual endpoint. Nanvaranak Choa remains a distinct mapped widening label.

scope_limits: Aphrewn River is a representative receiving-system candidate only; it does not replace Kashunuk River on upstream reaches or Nanvaranak Choa on the named widening.
The chosen opening and stored terminal are interior positions in the mapped channel network; neither is asserted as a natural source or ocean mouth.
The generalized selection cuts bends, islands and floodplain margins. The finding establishes connected corridor identity, not exact banks or individual rendered-segment waterways.
The maps do not establish current tidal direction, stage-dependent navigation or precise reach-name boundaries.
Formal naming-registry verification and Korean-name standardization have not been undertaken.

records.region: Falcón, northwestern Venezuela; possible Mitare receiving drainage
records.material_pending_reason: The usable regional chapter does not map the chosen headward opening, selected upper/middle branch sequence and joins, any selected reservoir/managed relation, or final deltaic channel to the actual terminal. These are ordinary corridor-scale evidence gaps; broad basin naming and coast geography do not complete them.
records.geographic_disambiguation: The chapter documents Mitare as a river reaching Golfete de Coro by Sabaneta and Mitare. Its correspondence to the complete selected route, including the upper branch and actual terminal, is not established.
records.completion_scope: Bounded research pass completed, but whole-feature geographic correspondence remains incomplete. All 50 selected parts of the one mainstem fragment were considered against the actual material obtained. The inspected regional map is thematic climate geography rather than channel evidence. No complete identity or completed naming-scope hold is claimed.
records.supported_name_scope: Regional prose identifies Río Mitare, also termed Mitare or Sabaneta in its mountain passage, and separately identifies Pedregal with Japure/Mamón and Paraíso with Juan Negro. None of the tributary names is assigned to an unverified selected part.

reconstruction_rule: Start from the pinned r46 cumulative index and apply later append-only deltas in verified commit order, rejecting duplicate IDs. Keep base records, scope clauses, region qualifiers and assessment histories unchanged. Apply explicit status-list changes. Subtract all recorded IDs from the exact eligible initial inventory to recover unrecorded targets; pending IDs remain recorded but are not completed source reviews.
publication_boundary: Own factual name/scope findings, public official URLs, bounded geometry metadata and public continuity pins only. No original maps, crops, complete coordinates or private source/derivative/registration fingerprints. Official hosting does not establish source redistribution rights.

research_order.progress_rule: Follow the actual continental order: Americas, Asia, Africa, Europe, then other, with all rivers before lakes. Preserve original queue IDs and ranks for continuity; apply documented geographic deferrals without counting them as name research, and place deferred objects into their corrected later phase by length-descending, stable-ID order. Prior candidate and scope-held assessments remain unresolved where stated.
